q: Name an infamous software bug, exploit or outage.

answers.l: Two-digit years everywhere. Billions were spent so that, on January 1, 2000, very little happened.
OpenSSL, 2014. A missing bounds check in TLS heartbeats leaked server memory. One of the first bugs with its own logo.
July 19, 2024. A faulty Falcon content update crashed about 8.5 million Windows machines.
December 2021. Log a crafted string and Log4j would fetch and run remote code via JNDI.
A radiation therapy machine, 1985 to 1987. A race condition with fast operator input caused massive overdoses.
Flight 501, 1996. Reused Ariane 4 code converted a 64-bit float to a 16-bit integer, which overflowed.
1999. One team used pound-force seconds, the other newton-seconds.
2018. Speculative execution leaks secrets through cache timing.
2018. Let user code read kernel memory on most Intel CPUs. Fixed by page-table isolation.
Discovered in 2010. A worm that sabotaged Iranian uranium centrifuges, using four Windows zero-days.
2017 ransomware, slowed when Marcus Hutchins registered its kill-switch domain for about $10.
November 1988. Infected about a tenth of the internet and led to the first felony conviction under the US Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.
1994. Missing lookup-table entries made some divisions slightly wrong. Intel took a $475 million charge.
2014. Bash ran code that trailed function definitions in environment variables. The bug dated to 1989.
March 2016. An 11-line npm package was unpublished and broke builds across the JavaScript world.
A signed 32-bit time_t overflows at 03:14:07 UTC on January 19, 2038.
An NSA SMB exploit leaked by the Shadow Brokers in 2017. It powered WannaCry and NotPetya.
A mistyped command removed too many servers in us-east-1. The status dashboard depended on S3 too.
October 2021. A BGP withdrawal took Facebook’s DNS off the internet for about six hours. Staff reportedly couldn’t badge into buildings.
2024. A years-long social-engineering campaign by "Jia Tan" hid a backdoor in xz’s test files.
May 2000. A VBScript email worm that reached tens of millions of Windows PCs.
2020. Attackers hid a backdoor in Orion software updates sent to about 18,000 customers.
2017. A wiper disguised as ransomware, spread through a Ukrainian accounting-software update.
2017. An unpatched Apache Struts flaw exposed data on about 147 million people.
1969. The guidance computer overloaded during the landing, restarted, and kept only the important jobs. The landing went on.
August 2012. Dead code was revived by a repurposed flag. $440 million lost in 45 minutes.
Dhahran, 1991. Time kept in tenths of a second drifted 0.34 s after 100 hours of uptime. 28 soldiers died.
1962. A missing overbar in a hand-transcribed guidance formula. Often misreported as a missing hyphen.
Apple, 2014. A duplicated "goto fail;" line skipped TLS signature checks.
Cloudflare, 2017. A parser bug leaked memory into responses that search engines then cached.
January 2003. A 376-byte UDP packet infected about 75,000 SQL Servers in around ten minutes.
2001. A worm hitting IIS servers, defacing pages with "Hacked By Chinese!"
2003. Its payload targeted windowsupdate.com and carried a message to Bill Gates.
1999. A Word macro virus that mailed itself to the first 50 contacts in Outlook.
Hammer one DRAM row and bits flip in its neighbors. A hardware bug with software exploits.
2016. A race in Linux’s copy-on-write let users write to read-only memory. Present since 2007.
January 2017. An engineer deleted the primary database’s data directory, and several backup methods turned out not to work. The recovery was livestreamed.
2014. The video’s view count neared 2^31 − 1, so YouTube moved to a 64-bit counter.
June 2021. One customer’s valid config change triggered a latent bug and knocked out much of the web for under an hour.
July 2019. A firewall rule with catastrophic regex backtracking pinned CPUs worldwide.
Oversized, fragmented ICMP packets crashed many 1990s operating systems.
Fujitsu’s Horizon accounting software showed false shortfalls, and hundreds of UK subpostmasters were wrongly prosecuted.
1997. Priority inversion kept resetting the lander. Engineers enabled priority inheritance in VxWorks, remotely.
January 15, 1990. A misplaced break in C switch software cascaded across AT&T’s long-distance network for nine hours.
A race condition stalled an Ohio utility’s alarm system, so operators missed the failure. 55 million people lost power.
December 31, 2008. 30 GB Zunes froze all day: a clock-driver loop never handled day 366.
2006 to 2008. A patch removed nearly all entropy, leaving only 32,767 possible keys per key type and architecture.
June 30, 2012. The leap second triggered a Linux timer bug that pinned CPUs at Reddit, Mozilla and more.
GPS counts weeks in 10 bits, so it wraps every 1024 weeks: August 1999, April 2019.
Excel treats 1900 as a leap year, deliberately, for compatibility with Lotus 1-2-3.
MySpace, 2005. An XSS worm that added a million friends in under a day. "but most of all, samy is my hero"
April 2022. A script meant to delete one app deleted whole customer sites. Some stayed down for two weeks.
October 2021. 73 hours down, traced to Consul under load and a BoltDB freelist problem.
Generator control units shut down after 248 days of continuous power: 2^31 hundredths of a second.
Windows 95 and 98 could hang after 49.7 days, when a 32-bit millisecond counter wrapped. Few machines stayed up that long.
February 29, 2012. Certificates valid for "one year from today" got the impossible date February 29, 2013.
